title: Data Collection Survey on the Application of Smart City Approach: Final Report

method_facts.fact: Urban issues, vision and strategy precede technology selection; local context conditions transfer.
Implementation needs named roles, finance, operational arrangements and monitoring.

source_limitations.text: The report principally concerns cooperation in developing-country cities. Its process concepts need local interpretation for central Tokyo.

title: A Data-driven Smart District Toward Net Zero Using Generative Design and Urban Digital Twins: A Use Case of Nihonbashi, Tokyo
citation_apa: Alorabi, A. H., Shen, J., Smith, J. M., Hawkins, M., Fatemifar, K., Yoshida, T., Murayama, A., & Yang, P. P.-J. (2025). A data-driven smart district toward net zero using generative design and urban digital twins: A use case of Nihonbashi, Tokyo. The International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences, XLVIII-4/W16-2025, 1–8. https://doi.org/10.5194/isprs-archives-XLVIII-4-W16-2025-1-2025

method_facts.fact: The three-stage framework connects a UBEM baseline, generated alternatives and interactive comparison; §3.3 uses URBANopt/OpenStudio/EnergyPlus.
Scenario variables include form, use, envelope/operation and renewable-energy assumptions.

source_limitations.text: The construction-year intervention rule is a scenario classification, not a verified structural or parcel decision for Kajicho. Review condition, ownership, whole-life carbon and planning feasibility before transfer.

title: Enhancing Urban Heat Risk Resilience in Tokyo’s Nihonbashi through Urban Digital Twins of 4-Step Scenario Planning
citation_apa: Zeng, Q., Nation, R. T., Ahmed, H. I., Ma, H.-C., Zhou, K., Gu, J., Yoshida, T., Murayama, A., & Yang, P. P.-J. (2025). Enhancing urban heat risk resilience in Tokyo’s Nihonbashi through urban digital twins of 4-step scenario planning. The International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences, XLVIII-4/W16-2025, 135–142. https://doi.org/10.5194/isprs-archives-XLVIII-4-W16-2025-135-2025

method_facts.fact: Four steps link description, evaluation, prediction and prescription through heat-index, network and vulnerability data.
The discussion distinguishes an envisioned stakeholder interface from current terminal/plot outputs and identifies static inputs and proxy limitations.

source_limitations.text: Traffic-density vulnerability proxy and static road/shelter data limit interpretation; shade/time-varying heat treatment needs development.
